```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Vignette code is executed locally (NOT_CRAN=true) but not on CRAN, where
# training would take too long and the CPU fallback could multi-thread.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"))
```

`rl_train()` runs any algorithm built with `rl_algo()` (PPO is one) for a
budget of environment steps, and handles what every run needs: evaluation,
logs, checkpoints, resume and reproducible RNG. Training is kept short here.

```{r}
library(rltoolsR)

env <- rl_vec_env("pendulum", n = 8, seed = 1)
algo <- rl_ppo(n_steps = 128, minibatch = 256, gamma = 0.9)
budget <- 8 * 128 * 4                  # 4 iterations
```

## 1. Evaluation during training

`eval_fn` is called with the current model every `eval_every_steps`
environment steps and returns a named numeric vector; `rl_evaluate()` fits
directly. Evaluation runs on its own RNG stream, so turning it on or off does
not change the training trajectory.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
m <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = budget, device = "cpu", verbose = FALSE,
              eval_every_steps = 2 * 8 * 128,
              eval_fn = function(model) rl_evaluate(model, "pendulum", n_episodes = 4))
m$eval
```

## 2. CSV logs

With `log = "run.csv"` every iteration is appended to `run.csv` and every
evaluation to `run_eval.csv` while training runs, so a long run can be watched
from outside R. Numbers are written in full precision.

```{r}
dir <- tempfile("rlt_")
dir.create(dir)
log <- file.path(dir, "run.csv")

set.seed(1)
m <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = budget, device = "cpu", verbose = FALSE,
              eval_every_steps = 2 * 8 * 128,
              eval_fn = function(model) rl_evaluate(model, "pendulum", n_episodes = 4),
              log = log)
head(read.csv(log), 3)
read.csv(file.path(dir, "run_eval.csv"))
```

An existing log is never overwritten silently: pass `overwrite = TRUE` to
start it again.

## 3. Checkpoints and resume

`checkpoint` writes the model with its whole training state: weights,
normalizer statistics, Adam moments, counters, both RNG streams, history and
evaluations. The file is written atomically, so an interrupted write keeps the
previous checkpoint. `checkpoint_every_steps` saves during the run as well.

```{r}
ck <- file.path(dir, "ck.rds")
set.seed(1)
m <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = budget, device = "cpu", verbose = FALSE,
              checkpoint = ck, checkpoint_every_steps = 2 * 8 * 128)
m$train_state$steps
```

`resume` continues from a checkpoint up to a larger budget. The environment is
reset, so an episode unfinished at the checkpoint is lost; everything else
continues where it stopped.

```{r}
m2 <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = 2 * budget, device = "cpu",
               verbose = FALSE, resume = ck)
nrow(m2$history)
```

A checkpoint is also a model file: `rl_load_model(ck)` reads it for
`rl_act()`.

## 4. GPU

`device = "auto"` trains on the GPU when a Vulkan device is available and on
the CPU otherwise; `"gpu"` and `"cpu"` force one. The network, the backward
pass and Adam run on the device; each update step is recorded once as a
captured ggmlR graph and replayed (`rl_ppo(capture = TRUE)`, the default).

```{r}
ggmlR::ggml_vulkan_available()
```

```{r, eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true") && ggmlR::ggml_vulkan_available()}
set.seed(1)
m_gpu <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = budget, device = "gpu", verbose = FALSE)
m_gpu$device
```

A small policy runs faster on the CPU: load models for acting with
`rl_load_model(path, device = "cpu")` (the default) and keep the GPU for
training, large batches and large networks.

## 5. Your own algorithm

An algorithm is a set of functions over a state that `rl_train()` passes
around: `init` builds it, `collect` steps the environment, `update` learns,
`model` returns what `rl_act()` / `rl_save_model()` use, and
`get_train_state` / `set_train_state` make it resumable. A random policy shows
the interface:

```{r}
random <- rl_algo("random",
  init = function(env, device) list(),
  collect = function(state, env) {
    r <- rl_step(env, stats::runif(env$n, -2, 2))
    list(state = state, steps = env$n, info = c(reward = mean(r$reward)))
  },
  update = function(state) list(state = state, metrics = NULL),
  model = function(state) list(meta = list()),
  get_train_state = function(state) list(optimizer_state = NULL),
  set_train_state = function(state, train_state) state)

env <- rl_vec_env("pendulum", n = 4, seed = 1)
rl_reset(env)
m <- rl_train(env, random, total_steps = 400, device = "cpu", verbose = FALSE)
head(m$history)
```

`collect` reports how many environment steps it took and an `info` vector;
`update` returns `metrics`. Both go into `history`, the CSV log and the
console, with the same names in every iteration.
